answer: The p-value for the null hypothesis that BMI is not associated with treatment response, from the multivariable (covariate-adjusted) binary logistic regression, is 0.1972 (two-sided Wald test on the BMI coefficient; BMI coefficient = 0.174, SE = 0.135, z = 1.29; OR = 1.19 per unit BMI, 95% CI 0.91-1.55). We do not reject H0: there is no statistically significant association between BMI and treatment response. (For reference, the unadjusted BMI-only Wald p = 0.0865 and the adjusted likelihood-ratio p = 0.188; the headline reported p is 0.1972.)
